hero_description: An overseas community service project organized by medical students from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore.
who_we_are_text:
Project Battambang was founded in 2010 by five Year 2 medical students under the mentorship of Dr Ong Yew Jin. What began as a small student-led initiative in Poipet has since grown into a long-standing overseas community involvement project committed to healthcare, education, and community engagement in Cambodia.

At the heart of Project Battambang is a belief in sustainable, locally grounded service. Beyond providing short-term support, we aim to listen closely, build lasting relationships, and strengthen existing community systems.
vision_text: We envision an independent community where everyone has the liberty and means to hope for and achieve a better future together.
mission_text: We resolve to improve the provision of healthcare and education through partnerships and supporting the local systems, and to empower youth to effect greater social awareness and responsibility within the community.
value1_desc: Serving with empathy and genuine care for the communities we meet.
value2_desc: Upholding ethical standards, transparency, and accountability in all operations.
value3_desc: Prioritizing the well-being and long-term health of our beneficiaries.
value4_desc: Listening closely to local needs and honoring Cambodian culture and partnerships.
value5_desc: Maintaining strict financial, clinical, and operational transparency.
value6_desc: Building enduring healthcare pathways and educational opportunities.
card1_description: Providing mass village health clinics, door-to-door screenings, chronic disease monitoring, and hospital referrals in Poipet.
card2_description: Investing in youth through the Light-A-Dream Scholarship, School Support Programme, and community hygiene education.
card3_description: Transparently documenting our annual trip findings, clinical statistics, financial statements, and community impact.
